qt: to the Commission Jean-Paul Garraud (PfE) Subject:

The Commission has been imposing significant financial sanctions on digital companies. The fines issued to Google illustrate just how much could be put towards the EU budget. While Member States are facing severe budgetary constraints, several European governments are calling for these revenues to be used to reduce their contributions to the EU budget, rather than to finance new expenditure. This matter is of particular significance to France, whose contribution for 2027 is estimated at almost EUR 31 billion, at a time when the country’s national public finances are deteriorating. Meanwhile, the Commission is proposing a substantial increase in EU expenditure for the period 2028-2034, accompanied by the creation of new own resources. In view of the above: 1.

Can the Commission provide the total sum of the fines imposed on large digital companies that the EU has actually cashed since 2020, and how much of this revenue has been used to reduce national contributions?
Will it propose a mechanism to ensure that exceptional revenue from competition fines is put as a matter of priority towards reducing Member States’ contributions to the EU budget?
How does it justify the creation of new own resources and the increase in the EU budget, given that extraordinary revenue could help to alleviate the burden borne by taxpayers in the Member States?
